summary: Classify inherited main storage and rules transitions in PR1877 semantic integration

replay.detail: Canonical projection catch-up still completes before requests are accepted.

schema.detail: The semantic merge adopts current main storage17 to19; it adds no migration of its own. Inherited checkpoint-memory17-to18 adds checkpoint_capture_epoch and guarded capture frontiers; inherited reconcile-start-preemption18-to19 adds runtime-start operation/evidence tables and admission indexes with retained launch evidence. See those existing fragments for their complete limits. Older binaries reject19; binary replacement does not undo these additive tables or retained evidence.

rules.detail: The semantic merge inherits main rules15 from retention-account-limits-rule.json: harness.limits and per-key reconcile decisions alter the retention digest. Checkpoint sealing/verification requires all participating members on15; no new rule is added by socket reservation.

compatibility.detail: Socket paths and discovery exist before store initialization, but listen and request acceptance remain after readiness. Startup clients retain connection refusal and the existing daemon-starting phase diagnostics. No queued initialization requests or client deadline changes. A per-address advisory lock protects bound-but-not-listening addresses and is retained during serving.

downtime.detail: Connection refusal and established-stream disconnects remain until initialization completes. Original early-listen connection-time measurements do not apply to this semantic port. No new startup latency or interruption budget is measured.

manual.detail: No socket configuration or manual SQL is introduced. This old PR integration adopts main storage19/rules15; preserve the normal coordinated fleet upgrade and forward-only database safety. Reservation sidecars are included in ordinary stopped-daemon uninstall.

recovery.detail: Roll forward through the existing main storage/rules upgrade route. Older17/18 binaries do not qualify rollback from19. Reservation file locks release on process exit but their files remain until ordinary stopped-daemon uninstall; no database state is erased by binary replacement.
